newsitem.title: UK: Lower non-OPEC supply gives extra room to OPEC - IEA.
newsitem.headline: Lower non-OPEC supply gives extra room to OPEC - IEA.

text.p: Oil supplies from non-OPEC producers will not hit the heights previously expected at the end of this year, leaving extra room for OPEC crude on world markets, the International Energy Agency said on Friday.

The Paris-based agency, in its monthly Oil Market Report, revised down its projections for supply from producers outside the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries for the third and fourth quarters of 1996 by 300,000 barrels per day (bpd).
"Primarily as a result of decreases in projections of non-OPEC supplies, the call on OPEC crude plus stock changes has been increased," the IEA said.
The IEA's third quarter call-on-OPEC oil projection was increased by 300,000 bpd to 24.2 million bpd and the fourth quarter estimate by 400,000 bpd to 25.6 million.
World oil production in August averaged 71.9 million bpd, down from July's 72.1 million bpd, said the IEA, which serves as the West's energy watchdog.

The IEA said output from non-OPEC producers dippped to 43.4 million bpd in August, reflecting reduced Latin American output following an explosion at a natural gas processing plant in Mexico and pipeline bombings in Colombia.
It said OPEC crude oil production last month averaged 25.81 million bpd compared to 25.88 million bpd in July.

Oil stocks held by industry in the Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) fell by 200,000 bpd in July -- the first time stocks fell in July for 11 years -- to stand 153 million barrels below the peak in 1995.

"However, stock levels decreased sharply in August 1995 and it is assessed that the 1996 stock shortfall versus year earlier levels was considerably less at the end of August than at the end of July," the agency added.
